title: CometBFT / Tendermint — protocol internals
description: Explanation layer for CometBFT cells (instrumentation.prometheus on :26660; standard cometbft_* names — live-verified at M5.2). Remember: client latency STRUCTURALLY includes block-interval wait — every figure says so.

panels.title: How to read a CometBFT run

options.content:
**Baseline expectation (corpus anchors: Buchman '18, Cason et al. — Tendermint commits in whole blocks on a ~1 s cadence; PaxiBFT measured ~1.7k tx/s class with enough clients):** height climbs ~1/s steadily on EVERY validator; rounds ≈ height (round >1 per height means a proposer needed retries — occasional is normal, persistent is stress); txs-per-block ≈ offered rate x block interval; harness p50 ≈ block interval (that is the protocol's latency SEMANTICS, not a bug — the 602 tx/s G1 run had p50 1.09 s).

**Fault runs:** kill a validator (n=4, f=1) → height keeps climbing with 3 signers, rounds may tick up briefly. DOUBLE_KILL (2 > f) is the intentional LIVENESS-LOSS demo: height FLATLINES — that flatline is the correct result, never 'fix' it. Proposer rotates every height, so faults target replica 0 by documented convention.

**Suspect signs:** height climbing but the harness reports errors → check tx validity (nonce/'=' rules — see CometBftDriver javadoc); one validator's height lagging → it is syncing, not signing (check its peers); block interval jumping around at fixed load → look at CPU steal before blaming consensus. If in-flight window / latency ≈ your measured TPS, you are WINDOW-bound (Little's Law) — raise --window, that ceiling is the client's, not the chain's.
